summary: The damage module, write-off flow and drawing are correct, and 40 of 41 checks pass. The one failed check, outsmarting_pays_more_than_stand_and_lunge, is a real defect. Starting a lunge makes the predicted dummy point overshoot the car. That drops `sees` and resets `senseTime`, so an aware, unsure car goes back to cruise speed. Standing in the lane and lunging therefore still pays the full 500, which is the exact behaviour CR-005 was meant to remove.

criteria.evidence: Checks load_sim and sim_is_pure. Source exports PARAMS, Damage, Vehicles, createSim and step, and has no Math.random, DOM or clock access.
Check params_match_spec (261 parameters identical). The PARAMS literal has the perception group and the CR-003 impact keys, and none of the removed keys.
Checks walk_frame_rate_independent (203.2 vs 202.8 px), run_speed_matches_spec and car_speed_real_time.
Check deterministic_and_seeded. rnd is called only in spawnStep; sensing, awareness and senseTime use no RNG. The wary, aware and senseTime fields are plain car fields in state.
Check attract_then_confirm. spawnStep returns at once when options.traffic is false.
Check lunge_distance_equal_8_directions (164.0 px in all eight) and lunge_frame_rate_independent. dummyStep sums an exact easeOutCubic difference.
Check held_lunge_does_not_chain (1 lunge). The fresh-press logic is in step() via prevLunge.
Check lunge_distance_equal_8_directions covers facing when no direction is held. In dummyStep, lungeDx uses facing unless a direction is held.
Check lunge_eases_out (87% at half time) and no_midair_steering.
Check recovery_is_tweened. dummyStep applies easeOutQuad over recoveryTime 0.35 s.
dummyStep clamps x and y to the hall every step, including during a lunge.
Check level1_road_flows_left_to_right. The road geometry in PARAMS is clear of the top-left corner; entry lanes start at 200.
Checks level1_road_flows_left_to_right (14 cars in 60 s) and traffic_audit L1 (longest stop 0 s).
Check level2_cross_no_collisions (18 horizontal, 24 vertical cars). drawEntry draws two approaches, left and top.
Checks level2_cross_no_collisions, level3_free_for_all and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play. axisMove truncates against every car.

The give-way loop in carsStep yields only to lower serials that are not behind the car. Check level2_cross_no_collisions (no deadlock). No dedicated scripted give-way check, so this rests on code reading.
Check level3_free_for_all (4 directions, 6 classes). drawEntry uses lateral bounds 200 to 520 and 200 to 800.
PARAMS.levels match. spawnStep respects the allocation, and the pool is limited by L.pool.
Check write_off_animation_then_card. writeOff() sets mode writeoff on the hit step and leaves card and ending null. dismiss() restores health.
Checks level_progression, ending_decommissioned and levelEnd() order. The level end is evaluated at the start of a play step.
Check ending_licensed. writeOffEnd calls finish('licensed') when bodiesDestroyed >= 11.
Checks tail_contact_pays_its_small_share and damage_module_is_logical (sedan tail 5/25). Reach is exactly 1 at full health.
Check html_static. index.html has no http:// or https://, uses a script tag for sim.js, and steps with a 1/60 accumulator. Font names come first with fallbacks.
Needs a person. The code draws roads, the level name and number, the HUD, cards, the attract screen and the restart button.
Playtest. Level end times are 62 to 97 s in levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic.
Check damage_in_play_matches_module. judge() calls Damage.assess once and applies res.damage to both score and health.
The damage_grid report matches the calibration for every class and zone. Largest single hit is 1174 < 1600.
Checks dummy_cannot_walk_through_a_car and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play. pushOut runs 4 passes with a clearance and a nearestClear fallback.
Cars read the dummy only through the sensing and reaction logic. Solidity enters only through pushOut, which never alters cars.
Checks solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play and vehicle_numbers_for_qa (barrier clearance minimum 9 px). latMove clamps to limits().
dummyStep has no barrier logic. Check solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play has the dummy wandering across the roads.
Commit and shoulder use are in the code via swFeasible and limits(). Check detection_commit_and_brake_flags shows VAN-07 locking. No explicit shoulder-entry count was reported.
Check levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic (dummy at the road edges). When neither side is feasible, `stuck` is set and the target becomes cruise*brake. The bus has canSwerve false.
latFree checks other cars' rectangles and, on level 3, oncoming bands. spawnStep waits on oncoming bands. Checks level3_free_for_all and solid_cars_and_barriers_under_active_play.
traffic_audit: L1 and L2 longest stop 0 s, and levels end within 98 s.
Playtest. drawBarriers and drawShoulders exist, with gaps at the level 2 crossing and nothing drawn on level 3.
Playtest.
Check level2_cross_no_collisions. Arrows are drawn in drawRoads for level 2.

Level 3 only. vehicle_audit reports the longest hold of the lowest-serial car at 13.5 s with a wandering dummy, above stallLimit+1 = 7 s. I cannot tell from the report whether the dummy was parked in that car's zone. See concerns.
Check levels_always_end_with_dummy_in_traffic (all ended). The breaker count on level 2 was 0 removals inside the hall.
stallStep is implemented to spec. No scripted check was reported; there is only the firing statistics.

The Damage object has exactly contactFace and assess and no references to state. Zone shares and the lunge multiplier appear only in Damage. judge() uses I.maxPay only to compute severity, as damage rule 6 allows.
Damage.contactFace follows the spec thresholds exactly (a > ha, |b| <= hb) and works for any heading.
damage_grid; my hand calculation below agrees. Check damage_module_is_logical.
assess is monotone in speed and zone, the lunge factor is a flat 5, and speed <= 0 gives mf 0 and damage 0. Check damage_module_is_logical.
Check damage_in_play_matches_module (diagonal flank lunge, van: 0.3 x 5 x 1.304 x 100 = 196). Direction and speed are not used in assess.
judge() records every lastImpact field. Check damage_in_play_matches_module.
judge() takes the zone from the snapshot position via outsidePoint and contactFace. Check hit_during_any_lunge_step_counts_as_a_lunge.
assess gives 0 when vs <= 0. judge() sets c.hit and levelContact and records lastImpact before returning on pay <= 0.
Check modules_exist_and_do_the_work. vehicle_audit: 400,536 car-steps, 7 over-limit steps, all attributed to truncation.
vehicle_audit: rest to cruise is 0.383 s for the sedan (equal to expected). Stop gaps are 7.8 to 7.9 px, all >= 0.
vehicle_audit: lane deviation 0 on all levels. traffic_audit: 0 cars removed inside the hall on L1 and L2.

All writes to car fields are in spawnStep, placeCar and carsStep. judge, writeOff and dummyStep only read cars; judge sets c.hit, which the spec allows. Vehicles has no writes to dummy, health or score.
The QA report is not part of the input. The orchestrator reports cover the damage grid, vehicle numbers, write-off numbers and breaker counts.
Playtest. The damage grid is logical.
PARAMS.writeOff.duration is 1.1.
writeOff() in sim.js sets mode, writeOff {t:0, duration, x, y} and the counters, and clears the lunge. Check write_off_animation_then_card.
The writeoff branch of step() only advances time and writeOff.t. Cars, the RNG and senseTime are untouched. Check write_off_animation_then_card (frozen).
Check write_off_animation_then_card (1.10 s). writeOffEnd sets the card, or finish('licensed') at 11 bodies.
prevConfirm is updated at the end of every step including writeoff steps, so a held confirm is not fresh. Check confirm ignored.
Needs a person. Code check in AC-62.

index.html reads wo.t/wo.duration for the shake amplitude 14*(1-u)^2, the red blend min(1,u/0.25), the smoothstep fade 0.35 to 0.85 (dummy gone from u=0.85), and 18 particles spawned at the first frame. Particle reach is below 120 px; particles are cleared when the writeoff ends. Math.random is used only in the renderer. sim.js has no shake or particle code.
Playtest.
PARAMS has maxHealth and maxPay at 1600; resetDummy uses maxHealth. No '2300' in sim.js.
Hand calculation: 500 per hit gives health 1100, 600, 100 and 0. Severity is 500/1600 = 0.3125. 16 walking hits of 100 write off the body.
The service rate in dummyStep is maxHealth/fullTime. Reach is 1-(0.55)(0.5) = 0.725 at 800.
Playtest. See AC-78.
The perception group in PARAMS matches the spec exactly. Check params_match_spec.
Check perception_geometry (9 points correct). senses() tests the path rectangle first, then the radius and the cosine at 80 degrees with a 1e-9 tolerance.

carsStep: senseTime += dt, aware = senseTime >= 0.15-1e-9, and it resets at once when sensing stops. Check reaction_delay_then_unsure_then_committed reports aware after 0.13 s (about 8 to 9 steps). Give-way and barriers do not read aware. The 0.13 s figure suggests the check starts counting after the first step; I could not confirm that.
Standing-dummy figures pass (69.0 and 82.8 in the checks). For a lunging dummy the 0.6 x factor never takes effect, because sensing is lost the moment the lunge starts. See defect 1.

Commit and flip both require c.aware. A locked car with a feasible swerve has target cruise; a locked car that is stuck gets cruise*brake. The bus has canSwerve false. Check reaction_delay_then_unsure_then_committed.
F is applied only in the aware branches (wary and unsure). The not-aware and locked-feasible branches use cruise. Check unnoticed_cars_ignore_the_dummy.
braking is true when speed fell, when the car is held, or when speed < cruise with target <= speed. A non-aware car's target is cruise, so no brake lights during the delay.

The failed check: stand-and-lunge reached the car at 138 px/s for 500. Case (a), standing in lane then lunging, must be 150 +/-25 and is 500. Cases (b) and (c) pay 500 as required. Cause is in defect 1.
sideRadius, sideHalfAngleDeg, reactionDelay and the speed factors are used only inside senses() and carsStep. Damage is unchanged and pure. No new RNG draws.

Playtest. drawCar draws the wedge from the nose, lit when c.wary. The path rectangle runs from the car centre for detect with half-width margin, lit when c.sees. drawAware draws a diamond with a 0.25 s ring, whether the overlay is on or off. Brake lights come from c.braking only.
By code: standing front-on and lunging still pays 500 (defect 1). The other points need a person.

defects.problem: In carsStep, `conflict` and `c.sees` are computed from the predicted point only. A lunging dummy has a predicted point about 470 to 490 px ahead (v about 1560 to 1640 px/s x predict 0.3 s), so on the first lunge step it lies far beyond the car's detect length. `sees` goes false. `c.wary` uses `senses(actual)==='side'`, which returns 'path' for an actual position in the path zone, so wary is false too. senseTime resets to 0 and aware drops. The aware, unsure car then goes back to cruise 138, so stand-and-lunge pays 500. This is the failed check, and it contradicts perception_and_reaction rules 7c and 9. It also means the caution factor F at s=1 never applies to a lunge at the nose.

`c.wary` is derived from senses(actual), which excludes the path zone. The spec defines wary as: sees false and the actual position inside the wedge. A dummy in the actual path zone but outside the predicted path zone is therefore neither sensed nor wary.

Locks are never released when the dummy leaves detection. The spec calls this the 'Testpad release rule', but the Testpad has no lock release either (lock stays set), so this is not a regression. It is a spec/behaviour mismatch to flag.

damage_audit.comment: All 20 values match my hand calculation of min(1600, round(100 x share x (5 if lunging) x speed x mass / 138)). Zone shares fall from nose to tail. Each lunging hit is 5 times the walking hit, up to rounding (for example bus tail 12 vs 59). Direction and lunge speed are never read by assess. A stopped car pays 0 because vs <= 0 gives 0. The largest hit is 1174 < 1600. judge() is the only place that reduces health or adds hit score; the write-off bonus is added in writeOff().

vehicle_audit.paths: Cars keep a fixed travel direction and stay on their lane line. Lane deviation is 0 on all levels with no dummy. The barrier limits are enforced in limits() and latMove. Measured minimum barrier clearance with a wandering dummy is 9 px. A car leaves its lane only by swerve, flip, or return to lane, each subject to swFeasible/latFree. Movement is truncated against every car by axisMove.
vehicle_audit.stop_start: A car slows or stops for these reasons: give-way to a lower-serial car, whose target is 0 or the speed of a same-lane leader; truncation against a touching car; the unsure and wary speed targets once aware; the Testpad brake factor, when the swerve is infeasible or the class is brake-first; and being held by latMove rejection. A car restarts when the yield target clears, accelerating at 360 px/s^2. Rest to cruise measured 0.383 s for the sedan, as expected. Following a stopped car, the cruise-to-stop time is 3.7 to 4.1 s and the stop distance 54 to 98 px. This is longer than cruise/decel because the car creeps in on its look-ahead; the gap at rest was 7.8 to 7.9 px, so no contact. Wary and unsure factors never go below 0.3 of cruise, so a dummy cannot stop a car. On L1 and L2 the longest stop was 0 s. On L3 the longest stop was 13.5 s.
vehicle_audit.removal: Cars are removed in two ways. Normal removal is when the rectangle is wholly out of the hall on its travel side: 81 of 87 on L1, 91 of 96 on L2, 102 of 108 on L3. The second is the stall breaker in stallStep, which deletes higher-serial cars adjacent to or in the sweep of a stalled lowest-serial car after 6 s with speed < 1 and sees false. It did not fire on L1 or L2. On L3 it removed 3 cars in 3 of 30 runs with an idle dummy and 4 cars in 3 of 30 runs with a wandering dummy. The breaker is a jam-clearing deletion, and a car has to be deleted to clear a jam. It is not a bug under this change, which does not touch it.
concerns: The L3 stall breaker fires in about 10% of runs. The longest hold of the lowest-serial car was 13.5 s, above the stallLimit+1 = 7 s bound in AC-39. This is outside CR-005 and is reported, not fixed.
On L3 a car stopped for 13.5 s, so jams do happen and are cleared by deleting cars.
The seven over-limit speed steps are all truncation, which the spec allows.

repair_requests.problem: A lunge makes the predicted dummy position overshoot the car, so sensing and awareness are lost exactly when the dummy lunges. The car returns to cruise speed and the stand-and-lunge hit still pays 500 (failed check outsmarting_pays_more_than_stand_and_lunge).
repair_requests.required_change: In carsStep, treat the dummy as sensed in the path zone when the predicted point OR the actual point (d.x, d.y) is in the path rectangle: `conflict = senses(predicted)==='path' || senses(actual)==='path'`. When only the actual point qualifies, use the actual along/lat for the commit line, the swerve preference and the brake factor B. Keep wary as: not conflict, and the actual position inside the wedge. Do not use senses() with its path-first return for wary. Then re-run the check; stand-and-lunge on a sedan should settle near 0.3 x 138 = 41 px/s and pay about 150 (+/-25). The ambush (500) and baited (500) cases must stay at 500.

repair_requests.problem: The spec's wary rule is not followed exactly.
repair_requests.required_change: Compute wary directly from the wedge geometry with sees false, so it does not depend on the path-first result of senses(). senses() itself must keep its AC-69 table behaviour.

notes: Builder notes say CR-005 was not run; the orchestrator checks did run and 40 of 41 passed. The only failure is the lunge-sensing defect.

The caution factor uses min(1, speed/runSpeed), so a walking dummy gives F = 0.8. This matches the Testpad. The spec's statement that s is 0 between walking and max should be corrected in the spec, not in the code.
The Testpad has no lock release, so the missing release in the build is not a regression. The spec's wording about a 'Testpad release rule' should be corrected.
The check reports 'aware after 0.13 s'. The code needs 0.15 s (9 steps at 1/60), so this is likely an off-by-one in how the check counts steps. It is worth confirming in the next run.
The renderer ring, wedge and path rectangle all draw from state.cars only. The awareness pulse is kept in a renderer-local map keyed by serial.
